To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a fully automated, integrated liquid‐phase platform for capturing/fractionation of fucosylation‐specific glycoproteins from human sera was developed.
we developed a fully integrated platform for capturing/fractioning fucome from human serum and we identified a broad panel of DEP and a narrow panel of commonly expressed DEP in breast cancer serum.

a fully integrated platform was designed for the simultaneous depletion and capture/fractionation of fucome from human disease‐free and cancer sera, and that the platform yielded a broad panel of differentially expressed proteins from breast cancer serum.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a novel integrated liquid‐phase platform operating in the cascade mode for the capture of fucome and its fractionation for comparative proteomic analysis of breast cancer and disease‐free sera.
the identification of the DEP in the serum of breast cancer patients using a novel integrated liquid phase platform.

the development of a fully integrated platform for the capture and fractionation of fucome from serum samples and the identification of DEP from breast cancer serum, which is a step towards the development of a diagnostic tool for early breast cancer detection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the developed platform is an excellent tool for the comparative proteomic profiling of disease‐free versus disease sera, yielding highly reproducible and accurate results, and is particularly useful in the identification of cancer‐specific biomarkers.

the platform is an efficient and effective tool for capturing/fractionation of the fucome from serum and for the subsequent comparative mass spectrometry‐based analysis of the fucomes from cancer and disease‐free sera.
the integrated multicolumn platform operating “in cascade” was successfully developed and utilized for the comparative mass spectrometry of fucome from breast cancer and disease‐free sera.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the platform developed in this work is a powerful tool for capturing/fractionation of fucome from complex serum samples.

we developed a fully integrated liquid phase multicolumn platform for fucome capturing/fractionating that allows the “cascaded” processing of the serum sample between the various columns in the liquid phase, thus minimizing experimental biases and sample loss and facilitating comparative mass spectrometry of disease‐free serum and breast cancer serum.
a fully automated platform for fucome isolation and fractionation has been developed, which is based on an integrated multicolumn approach and is operated in the liquid phase in “cascade”.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a fully integrated platform operating in cascade in the liquid phase, with the simultaneous subtraction of high abundance serum proteins and the capturing of the fucome, is a powerful tool for the identification of cancer biomarker candidates.
the integrated liquid‐phase platform is a valuable tool for the analysis of fucome from complex biological matrices such as sera.

the platform developed can be utilized for the comparative analysis of disease sera, and that it allows for the capture of a broad range of fucosylation changes in the serum glycoproteinome of breast cancer.
